transcript: THE Patti Lupone and THE Mia Farrow are back on Broadway together and honestly I could probably stop the video there but I'm not gonna the play is called The Roommate by Jen Silverman and it's been kind of kicking around in regional theaters for the last like 10 years or so but it's finally making its New York debut and Jen Silverman is making their much deserved Broadway debut the Roommate is definitely a bit more traditional compared to the other two plays that I've seen from Jen Silverman but it still has kind of a kooky flair to it it starts off just seeming like a classic odd couple situation comedy but then it has a lot of twists and turns along the way that you wouldn't expect The show definitely got some good laughs out of me it is for the most part a comedy but I will say it also kind of struck some emotional chords for me that I wasn't expecting I really kind of resonated with these themes of like second acts in life and the family dynamics that we see in particular I found it to be a really effective character study of Sharon the character that Mia Farrow plays and that is in no small part owed to Mia Farrow’s pretty magnificent performance she really more than anything else in this production was cracking me up and breaking my heart Patti LuPone is definitely very grounded I mean her technical acting skills are obviously very strong but I couldn't shake the feeling that she didn't quite nail the essence of this character the way that Mia Farrow did with her role overall I wouldn't call this any sort of groundbreaking piece of theater but for me it hit most of the right notes and honestly even if you're on the fence about the play itself I would still say that it's worth it for Mia Farrow’s performance
